summary:
Trabzon province generates no trans-specific statute, enforcement pattern or incident documentation in the available record. What is recorded for Trabzon is the absence of any documented divergence from the national position, which is not a finding of safety: the Turkish national framework extends to Trabzon in full, and a visitor to the province should expect the same legal exposure, document checks and detention practice documented elsewhere in Turkey.

HRW reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked omnibus reform draft, the 11th Judicial Package, would amend the Turkish penal code to punish conduct "contrary to biological sex" with up to three years in prison, and participation in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony with up to four years. The draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care including surgery from 18 to 25, mandate permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals, and expose both healthcare professionals performing such care and patients to criminal prosecution, with pretrial detention possible. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft; HRW calls for its withdrawal. Whether the package has since passed is unresolved in the sources.

Kaos GL's Human Rights Report 2025, titled "The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People", finds LGBTI+ hostility became explicit state policy, with instructions issued to public institutions under the "Year of the Family" banner. It documents 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings with trans people the most affected, 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (a striking increase over the prior year), 313 right-to-liberty violations — about 2.5 times the previous year — with 299 detention decisions, freedom-of-expression violations rising from 216 to 540, and 40 right-to-association violations including the first closure of an LGBTI+ association in many years. These figures are national totals reported without a provincial breakdown, so they cannot be attributed to Trabzon specifically; they indicate the enforcement climate a visitor to the province would enter.
tangentialFactors:
The national monitoring totals are counted as raw violations over the year, not per capita or per region, and the source provides no denominator by province; Trabzon's share of the 313 recorded violations is not stated and cannot be inferred.

The draft 11th Judicial Package sits within a broader pattern of family-and-morals framing used by the national government, per HRW and Kaos GL, which shapes the political climate in every province including Trabzon.
localsOnly: Residents of Trabzon province live under the same national legal framework as visitors, with no provincial statute or local protection instrument recorded in the sources. The Kaos GL figures on detentions, torture/ill-treatment and association closures apply to residents as well as visitors, and no Trabzon-specific enforcement or complaint data appears in the record.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since HRW's 29 October 2025 report is unresolved in the sources.

No Trabzon-specific incidents, police practice, healthcare access data or facility rules are sourced; the province's position is inferred from the absence of divergence rather than from positive local documentation.
